Severe label collisions: 'Pit stop record'/'Human reaction time' overlap (f10, f12), 'Modern crew'/'1950s crew' overlap the source line (f11), and three stacked source lines pile onto the 'COMMENT BELOW' CTA at f18–f20.
Bar values are ghosted, clipped or hidden — '.9'/'.8' cut off behind the mascot (f09), '0.3' clipped at the pill edge (f12), '20'/'3' still ghost-faded at f17.
fixes: Open on the 1.8s stop actually happening — a car dropping onto the jack with a timer snapping to 1.80 in the first 12 frames — instead of an empty chart and a title.
Remove the house icon from the 'Current record' bar; use a tyre/stopwatch glyph or nothing.
Rebuild seg3 as twenty Data figures swarming a car versus three in the 1950s lane, filling the upper frame; keep the bar comparison for only one beat in the video.
Give Data a per-beat pit-crew act with setup→action→payoff: wheel gun spinning off a nut, jack slamming down, lollipop lifting — never the same pose twice.
Fix the label layout: stagger or shorten the two axis labels so they cannot overlap each other or the source line, and collapse the three end-card source lines into one line clear of the CTA.
Hold the camera so titles and right-edge labels stay in frame, and resolve every bar value to full opacity before its beat ends.

one_line: A competent bar-race buried under an irrelevant house icon, caption-over-chart collisions, and a mascot that just rides the bar instead of performing the stat.
auto_fails: junk_imagery: A house/home building icon sits on the 'Current record' bar cap from hook@0.3 through seg1:end (f00-f09) — a residential house has nothing to do with an F1 pit stop, and at seg1:start it is a garbled cutout half-clipped by the bar.

decorative_mascot: From seg2:start through seg4:end (f10, f13, f15, f17, f19) Data stands centered on the yellow bar in an identical arms-out/arms-up idle with no setup->action->payoff tied to 1.8s vs 0.27s or 20 vs 3; he is a sticker riding the bar, not performing.
problems: hook@0.3-2.2 (f00-f06): a house/home icon on the 'Current record' bar is unrelated to F1 pit stops and is the first thing in frame alongside the mascot.
hook@0.3-2.2: the oversized burned-in caption is drawn across the 1950s bar, and the yellow 'Current record' label overprints the mascot — three layers colliding in one band.
seg2:start/seg2:end (f10, f12): the axis labels collide into 'Pit stop recordHuman reaction time', and the source line runs underneath them.
seg2:end/seg3:end (f12, f15): the bar values (1.8, 0.3, 20, 3) are rendered in low-contrast grey inside the bars and are partly hidden behind the mascot at seg1:end (f09: '60', '.9', '.8' clipped).
seg3:mid (f14): the zoom crops 'Modern crew' / '1950s' labels off the right edge and the source line runs off frame.
seg2 through seg4 (f10, f13, f15, f17, f19): the mascot repeats the same standing arms-out idle on the yellow bar with no bit tied to the reaction-time or crew-size comparison.
fixes: Drop the house icon from the 'Current record' row (or swap it for a pit-lane/tyre/stopwatch mark) so no off-topic imagery appears in the first 2s.
Move the hook caption to the lower third and add a collision offset so row labels never overprint the bars or the mascot.

Give the mascot one real bit per comparison: have him physically drop the jack / spin four wheels off and be gone before the pink reaction-time bar finishes filling, instead of standing on the bar cap.
Raise bar-value contrast and draw values outside/above the bar cap so 60, 1.8, 0.3, 20 and 3 are never occluded by the mascot.
Constrain the seg3:mid zoom so both category labels stay inside the safe area.
Fill the empty upper column area — start the vs-columns from the top or add a countdown/tick element there — so the frame's top half carries motion.

one_line: The 2%-vs-98% payoff scene — the whole point of the video — is illegible: its two bar labels are printed on top of each other and run off the frame.
auto_fails: decorative_mascot: Data has no setup->action->payoff bit: he perches on whatever shape is nearest and slides — atop the 105 bubble at seg1:start, leaning on the Millennials bar at seg2:start, standing on the purple bar at seg3:start, then drifting down it unchanged across seg4:start/mid/end.
problems: seg3/seg4: the two bar captions overlap into unreadable text and collide with the source credit line, destroying the video's central comparison
seg3: the kicker 'WEALTHIEST 2% OF HOUSEHOLDS VS THE OTHER 98%' is cut off by the right edge of the frame
seg3/seg4: the pink 98% bar carries no number, so the 'equal to the other 98% combined' equality is never shown — only the purple bar gets a '62'
Mascot never performs a bit: across all six scenes he only perches on or slides down whichever shape is on screen, with no setup->action->payoff tied to any stat
hook@0.3: opens on a near-empty title card with a tiny idle mascot and one stray dot — the bubbles only start growing after ~0.8s, so frame one gives no reason to stay
seg4:start-end: the closing ~4s is a near-frozen bar chart with a speech bubble; measured duplicate_ratio 0.263 / effective 17.7fps shows judder rather than purposeful motion
fixes: Constrain each comparison label to its own bar column with wrap/shrink-to-fit and move both above the source credit so 'Wealthiest 2%' and 'The other 98%' never overlap; clamp the kicker to the card's safe width
Label BOTH bars with $62T and animate them rising to the identical height in sync so the equality lands visually
Give Data a real bit in seg3: have him try to carry the 2% bar's stack, stagger, and get flattened as the 98% bar matches it — setup, action, payoff
Replace the static hook with immediate motion: start the $124T mass already splitting into the 105/18 bubbles on frame one instead of a title card
Re-cut the final 4 seconds so something purposeful moves under the closing card — e.g. the 62 counting up or the bars settling — instead of holding a duplicated frame

one_line: An honest, well-sourced race with a real leaderboard flip at 2023 — but the hook card sits illegibly on top of the chart and the label/flag collisions in the middle third make it read amateur.
problems: hook@0.3-1.5: hook banner occludes the China line and its axis label, then fades to unreadable dark gold on black while still on screen.

mid4/mid5 (2020, 2021): the 'China 1.4B' and 'India 1.4B' text labels and their flag markers collide and overlap each other at the converging tips — the exact moment the video's whole claim rests on is the messiest frame in it.
The overtake never reads visually: at payoff@-1.8 the two lines are still stacked and only the leaderboard order and the '#1 India' caption at payoff@-0.4 announce the flip.
mid0-mid2: the plot's entire lower half and right half are empty black while both series crowd the upper-left — the frame is composed for the 1950s and never rebalances.
Title wraps to two lines over the leaderboard, eating the top ~15% before the chart starts.
fixes: Reposition the hook text into the empty lower-left of the plot area and give it a solid/high-contrast plate so it stays legible for its full duration and never covers a series.
Add collision avoidance to the tip labels: when two series are within ~5% on the y-axis, stagger the labels vertically (or offset one leftward) so the flags and text never overlap at the crossover.
Stage the overtake — hold a beat at 2022-2023, flash the crossing point, and animate the leaderboard rows swapping so the pass is something you SEE, not something the caption tells you.
Auto-zoom the y-axis to the active data band (or pan the x-window with the leading tip) so the early years don't render as a chart in the corner of a black field.
Trim the ~1.1s frozen tail at 13.25s or replace it with a final beat (delta callout, '+X since 1950') so the video ends on a move, not a still.

one_line: A genuinely good two-series race with a real crossover, wasted by a dead, glitchy first two seconds and a '#1' payoff pinned on a series that is itself collapsing.
problems: hook@0.3: opens on an empty chart with one tiny stub — the classic slow chart build the rubric forbids as an opener.
hook@0.8 / hook@1.5: the hook caption fades into an illegible dark-yellow smear over black; it looks like a bug, not a transition.

payoff@-0.4: the closing badge reads '#1 E-Cigarettes 8' while the green line has fallen from 27 to 8 — crowning a declining series undercuts the 'one habit replaced another' thesis and lands no whoa.
mid5 t=12.38s to payoff@-0.4 t=13.97s is near-identical (max duplicate run 1.04s at 13.33s); the tail coasts instead of building.
Title wraps to two lines and crowds the leaderboard directly beneath it, squeezing the plot area in the early frames.
fixes: Pre-roll the race so the first visible frame is already near the 2014 crossover, or cold-open on the end-state for ~0.5s then rewind to 2011.
Render the hook caption at full opacity with its dark plate for its whole duration — no fade-to-brown; if it must exit, cut or slide it off rather than dissolving it.
Change the closing badge from '#1 E-Cigarettes' to the actual scale payoff: cigarettes 16% → 1%, and call out that vaping peaked at 27.5% and is now falling too.
Add a marked beat at the crossover year (2015/2016) — pause the year counter for a half-second and flash the swap in the leaderboard so the moment one habit overtook the other is unmissable.
Tighten the tail: hold the final state for under a second and let the closing line land on motion rather than a frozen chart.

one_line: A clean, legible race that only tells half its title: the humpback boom is beautifully drawn, but the vanishing whale is a flat red line on the axis, so the promised contrast never actually happens on screen.
problems: mid0-payoff: the N. Atlantic Right Whale series is crushed to the zero line by the shared 100K axis — its 475->356 decline, the 'vanishing' in the title, is invisible in every single frame.
hook@0.3-hook@2.2: the opener is the thing the rubric names outright — a plain title card plus a slow chart build; nothing surprising happens in the first two seconds beyond a line starting to climb.

hook@1.5: the 'Same ocean, opposite fates' chip fades out as dark gold on near-black over the plot area and is briefly illegible mid-fade, reading as a rendering artifact rather than a deliberate transition.
mid3 (t=8.43s): the 'N. Atlantic Right Whales 475' label runs into the right edge of the frame and is clipped.
payoff@-0.4: the ending crowns '#1 Humpback Whales' — a competitive-winner card on what is a scale-and-divergence story, and it lets the second whale exit the video unmentioned.
Cadence is soft: duplicate_ratio 0.262 gives an effective 17.7fps, with a ~1.0s held run at t=13.33 right before the final card.
fixes: Put the right whale on a readable scale — log y-axis, a normalised index (1991 = 100), or a small inset panel that tracks it alone — so its rise to 475 and fall to 356 is a visible shape by mid2.
Open on the divergence instead of the build: pre-draw both curves to their 2023 endpoints in the first 0.5s, snap back to 1991, then race — the viewer sees the gap before they see the title.
Hold the hook chip on a solid card with full-opacity text and cut it, rather than cross-fading it into the plot where it turns to unreadable dark gold.
Inset the leaderboard/tip labels by ~24px so 'N. Atlantic Right Whales 475' cannot clip the frame edge at mid3.
Replace the '#1 Humpback Whales' end card with the comparison the title promised — '96,000 vs 356' or 'one recovered 10x, one is down to 356' — so the payoff lands both fates.
Raise the tween density on the year interpolation to remove the 0.26 duplicate ratio and the ~1s freeze at t=13.33.

one_line: Clean, well-sourced graph race with a genuinely dramatic 121M->2M collapse, let down by a static hook and a y-scale that buries the crossover in the bottom eighth of the frame.
problems: hook@0.3-0.8: hook card sits on a blank chart with no motion behind it, and it covers the Compact Cameras 113.1M tip label.
hook@1.5: hook text does not clear — it lingers as a ghost across the 100M gridline while the chart is already animating.

mid2-mid5 (t=6.45-12.38s): with the gray line down at 22M and below, all the action compresses into the bottom ~15% of a plot whose axis still reaches 140M; the entire 40M-140M band is dead space for the back half of the video.
payoff@-0.4: the finish resolves to a '#1 Interchangeable-Lens' banner, which is the wrong punchline for a collapse story — 8M 'winning' reads flat next to the 121M->2M wipeout the chart just drew.
mid3 (t=8.43s): at the crossover, the two tip images and their labels collide in the same 20M band, so the single most important moment of the story is the most cluttered frame in it.
fixes: Start the race pre-rolled or fast-sweeping under the hook card so hook@0.3 has visible line motion, and hard-cut the hook text off by ~1.2s instead of fading it over the gridlines.
Move the hook card into the empty upper-right region so it never overlaps a series tip label.
Add a late y-axis rescale (or a log/zoom transition around 2016) so the crossover and the final 8M vs 2M gap fill the frame instead of hugging the axis.
Reframe the ending on the collapse, not the winner: hold on '121M -> 2M, -98%' with the compact-camera tip visibly bottoming out, and demote the #1 banner to a subtitle.
At the crossover year, stagger the two tip labels vertically (one above, one below the line) and briefly flash the swap so the moment reads instead of overlapping.

one_line: The last twelve seconds are a frozen, off-topic food-delivery screenshot and the story ends mid-sentence, so the payoff never lands.
auto_fails: junk_imagery: mid4/mid5/payoff@-1.8/payoff@-0.4 (t=44.4-56.5s) all show a SkipTheDishes food-delivery 'Order Feedback' laptop screenshot over captions about a logo, an account and an invoice — wrong topic entirely; mid3 (t=33.9s) is a blank aged parchment with no content.

dead_air: The top half is the identical SkipTheDishes still at mid4 (44.4s), mid5 (54.9s), payoff@-1.8 (55.1s) and payoff@-0.4 (56.5s) — four beats visually identical for the final ~12s, even though motion facts show the gameplay strip below keeps moving (longest_static_s 0.0).
problems: hook@0.3-hook@0.8: the opening is a static Reddit title card over near-black gameplay with no illustration and nothing happening — no reason to stop scrolling.
mid4 through payoff@-0.4: a single irrelevant SkipTheDishes 'Order Feedback' screenshot fills the top half for the final ~12s across four beats.
mid3 (t=33.9s): the illustration is a blank aged parchment — no visible content tied to 'OF HER LIVE'.
mid2 (t=23.5s): a padlock on a 'Professional Standards' document is only loosely connected to the logo/licensing beat.
payoff@-0.4 ends on the caption 'TRACED BACK TO' — the video stops mid-clause with no punchline or resolution.
fixes: Open on a concrete visual — the stolen logo appearing on someone else's storefront/product — and animate it in during the first 0.5s, with the post card sliding in over it rather than sitting on black.
Cut the tail into separate on-topic shots: the reused logo spotted in the wild, an itemised licensing invoice, and the payment/climbdown; never hold one illustration past ~4s.

Drop the SkipTheDishes screenshot and the blank parchment from the shot pool for this script; require the chosen image to contain the beat's subject noun (logo, invoice, contract), not just a caption keyword.
Extend the final beat so the closing sentence completes on screen and the last caption is the punchline, not a dangling preposition.

one_line: Clean, always-moving reddit-story build, but two of the six illustration shots (a charm necklace, an antique apothecary) have nothing to do with a coffee-shop upsell, and the ending holds the worst of them while the punchline caption never completes.
auto_fails: junk_imagery: mid3 (t=32.0s) shows a silver dog-tag/charm necklace on wood while the caption reads 'THE DISTRICT MANAGER'S', and mid5/payoff@-1.8/payoff@-0.4 hold an antique apothecary shelf of glass bottles — neither belongs to a coffee-shop retail story.
problems: mid3 (t=32.0s): silver dog-tag necklace photo under the caption 'THE DISTRICT MANAGER'S' — no connection to the story beat.
mid5/payoff (t=51.67-53.27s): antique apothecary bottle shelf held across the entire closing beat, unrelated to the retail/coffee setting.
Payoff never lands visually: payoff@-1.8 shows the caption cut mid-phrase at 'CARD HE NEVER' and payoff@-0.4 has no caption and no new image.

Inconsistent grade across illustrations — mid2 (t=22.17s) and mid4 (t=41.83s) are desaturated black-and-white while mid1, mid3 and mid5 are full colour, so the top panel reads as scraped rather than art-directed.
hook@0.3-2.2: the post card is the only hook device; the top panel is empty of story imagery for the first 2.5s, so the opening is carried entirely by the gameplay lane.
fixes: Re-source the mid3 shot to something in the story's world — a barista at a register, a manager badge/lanyard, a chain-store storefront — and gate shot selection on subject match, not keyword overlap.
Give the final segment its own illustration of the punchline object (loyalty card, receipt, POS screen) and hold it no longer than the beat it belongs to.
Extend the closing caption so the full final sentence appears before the last frame, and land the final beat on the payoff image rather than the previous scene's still.
Normalise colour treatment across all top-panel shots — pick colour or desaturated for the whole video, not per-shot.
Put a story image or a punched-in detail shot in the top panel during the hook so the first 2s carries the premise visually alongside the post card.

one_line: Clean, well-sourced chart work with real continuous motion, but the frame goes hollow in the population scene and Data is a passenger on the graphics for most of the runtime instead of a performer.
auto_fails: decorative_mascot: Data never runs a setup->action->payoff bit: he stands inside the green pill doing nothing at seg2:start/mid/end, then perches on top of the 2024 bubble from seg3:mid through payoff@-0.4 (~14s) with only idle pose jitter — he rides the composition rather than acting on the stat.

empty_void: seg3:start (t=29.53s) is a near-empty 'demand vs supply' panel — a pinhead 3.3 dot on the right, a small mascot mid-frame, and the entire upper half plus right third dead; seg3:mid still leaves the top ~40% blank with two small circles low in the frame.
problems: seg3 wastes the frame: at seg3:start a single tiny 3.3 dot and a sub-pixel green circle sit in a mostly empty panel, and at seg3:mid the top ~40% is still blank.
Data has no bit anywhere — he stands inside the pill at seg2:start/mid/end and perches on the 2024 bubble from seg3:mid to payoff@-0.4 (~14s) with only idle jitter; no setup->action->payoff.
Hook is a chart build, not an event: hook@0.3 through hook@2.2 is bars growing under a title card, so the first two seconds give a stranger no reason to stop.
Text collisions: the source footer runs straight through the '1963'/'Today' labels at seg2:start and seg2:end, and through 'COMMENT BELOW' at seg4:end.
Bar value labels are clipped by their own bars at seg1:end — '2,000' reads as '000' and '1,350' as '350'.
The closing (payoff@-1.8 to payoff@-0.4) holds one composition for ~5s with only mascot idle motion, so the 95%-collapse punchline lands softly.
fixes: Rebuild seg3 so the bubbles fill the panel — scale the 2024 circle to dominate the upper-middle with 1963 adjacent for contrast, and drop the '6x the mouths, a fraction of the water' line into the empty upper band.

Give Data one real act per scene tied to the stat: bailing water out of the shrinking 1987 bar in seg1, being squeezed as the 100% pill collapses to 5% in seg2, being shoved aside by the expanding 2024 bubble in seg3.
Replace the hook with an immediate event — snap the 1963 bar to full and let it visibly drain/collapse toward 2001 within the first second, rather than growing all four bars from zero.
Raise the source footer above the year-label row (or move it inside the panel edge) so it stops overlapping '1963'/'Today' and 'COMMENT BELOW'.
Render bar value labels outside the bar end once the bar is shorter than the label width so '2,000' and '1,350' stay fully legible at seg1:end.
Add a final beat to the payoff: shrink the 1963 lake silhouette down to the 5% remnant behind the closing card so the last 5s carries motion into the CTA.

one_line: Genuinely good chart choreography with the mascot riding and shoving the data, undercut by a seg1 punch-in that crops the title off-frame and tears the bar edges.
problems: seg1:mid (t=9.59s): zoom crops the title, the subtitle and half the mascot out of frame, and horizontal tearing artifacts cut across the pink/purple band edges.
seg2:start (t=17.77s): same over-zoom problem — the '2018' label is clipped to '20' at the right edge and the top third is dead unfilled ghost bars.

seg2:start/seg3:start: the burned-in caption and the big green stat ('80 percent of' over '80%', '91.8 percent in' over '91.8%') stack into a two-line clutter block that repeats the same number twice.
A stray cyan ellipse floats untethered in seg2:start (t=17.77s) and seg3:start (t=30.48s) with no visible connection to a data point or a mascot action.
The three beats are three different chart types with no visual through-line — the stacked-band metaphor set up in seg0/seg1 is abandoned rather than paid off.
fixes: Clamp the seg1 and seg2 camera moves to a title-safe box so the chart title, every year label and the full mascot remain in frame; snap the zoom scale to stop the band-edge tearing.
Suppress the redundant big stat overlay when the spoken caption already contains the same number, or move it to the opposite third of the frame so the two never stack.
Attach the cyan ellipse to something — the data point being called out or a prop in the mascot's hand — or drop it.
Fill seg2:start's empty upper third by starting the 1983/2018 bars taller in frame or pulling the 'VS' and year labels up into that space.

one_line: Solid data metaphors and a mascot who actually rides the numbers, wrecked by a final act whose labels overprint into unreadable text and whose 2%-equals-98% punchline never visually lands.
problems: seg3/seg4: category labels 'Wealthiest 2% of households' and 'The other 98% of households' render on the same baseline and overlap into illegible text for the last 16 seconds of the video.
seg3/seg4: the header subtitle is cut off by the frame edge, reading 'WEALTHIEST 2% OF HOUSEHOLDS VS THE OTHER 98¢'.

seg4: the payoff figure 62 is drawn in dim grey inside the purple bar and is barely readable at payoff@-0.4; the other side has no matching number at all, so the 'same as the other 98% combined' equivalence is asserted in narration only.
The source credit line collides with the axis labels in seg1:mid and with the category labels in seg3:mid.
seg2:start: the generation bars carry no value labels while the mascot straddles the Gen X bar, so $46T/$39T/$15T are never shown at the moment they are spoken.
Mascot bits stop at perch-and-lean -- he never completes a setup -> action -> payoff gag; in seg3/seg4 he stands on one bar for 16s with only idle leg motion.
fixes: Wrap or shorten the two seg3 category labels and center each under its own bar; add a width-fit pass so no two labels share a baseline.
Truncate or shrink the seg3 subtitle to the card safe area so it does not clip at the right edge.

Restyle the seg3/seg4 value as high-contrast white/near-white type and show $62T on BOTH bars simultaneously, with a brief snap/flash when the two heights match, so the equality is the visual punchline.
Move the source credit to a reserved bottom band below the plot area so it never overlaps axis or category labels.
Add value chips ($46T / $39T / $15T) to the seg2 generation bars, revealed as each is named, and offset the mascot so he does not cover the Gen X bar.
Give Data one real bit in seg3: have him try to drag the 98% bar higher than the 2% bar, fail, and slump on top of it as the two lock level.

one_line: Honest, well-sourced chart work, but it opens on a slow empty-bar build with captions crashing into the row labels, and Data spends 40 seconds standing in bars instead of performing a bit.
auto_fails: decorative_mascot: Same 'stand on / inside the bar' motif for the whole run — he perches on the 2021 row (hook@1.5), stands inert inside the blue Buybacks column (seg2:start, seg2:mid, seg2:end) and again at seg3:start–seg3:end, with no setup→action→payoff tied to the 806 vs 456 gap.
problems: hook@0.3 / hook@0.8: caption 'Dividends used' overlaps the 2007 year label and bar; hook@1.5 / seg0:mid: 'to be' sits inside the 2007 bar — the opening two seconds are a title card over empty tracks.

Mascot has no bit tied to the data: he perches on the 2021 row (hook@0.8), then just stands inside the Buybacks column at seg2:start, seg2:mid, seg2:end, seg3:start and seg3:mid — position changes, purpose does not.
seg4:start through payoff@-0.4: the mascot's head and torso are clipped behind the closing callout box, leaving a headless pair of legs on every payoff frame.

Source attribution line collides with the 'Buybacks' / 'Dividends' axis labels at seg2:end, seg3:end and payoff@-0.4, and a second duplicated source block is stacked below the card at seg4:start and seg4:end.
seg3:start holds nearly two-thirds of the panel as empty track above two short columns with only 'VS' in it — the frame's space is underused at the moment the comparison should be strongest.
Cadence is soft: effective 20.6 unique fps against a 24fps sample, with a 1.0s frozen run at t=47.46 landing exactly on the payoff.
fixes: Reserve a caption safe zone in the lower third for the hook the way seg1+ already do, and never let caption text render over chart rows or year labels.
Start the hook mid-event — the 2025 bar already blasting past 1 trillion, or the finished ranking snapping in and rewinding — instead of growing all five bars from zero.

Give Data one real bit per beat with setup→action→payoff: have him try to catch a falling dividend check that shrinks while the buyback bar shoves him across the frame at seg2, rather than standing inside the column.
Raise the closing callout or drop the mascot's anchor ~120px at seg4 so he is fully visible next to the payoff instead of decapitated by the speech bubble.
Move the source line below the axis labels with real padding, and delete the duplicated source block rendered outside the card at seg4.
Scale the seg3 columns to fill more of the panel height, or push the camera in, so the 2021 comparison does not read as two short pills under a large empty area.

one_line: Real sourced numbers in a clean house style, but the back half is the same two-column card twice with a decorative — and at the end upside-down — mascot and text collisions.
auto_fails: decorative_mascot: He rides/perches on the leading bar with no setup→action→payoff: seg2:mid, seg3:start and seg3:mid are the same 'stand on top of the blue column' pose, and by payoff@-1.8/seg4:end he is a tiny upside-down sticker clipped behind the caption box.
problems: Hook opens on a slow bar build, and the caption 'Dividends used to be' covers the 2007 row label at hook@0.3/hook@0.8 — the first frame is a chart loading, not an event.
seg3 is a near-copy of seg2's composition (same title, columns, VS glyph), so beats 2 and 3 read as one repeated card.
The mascot performs no bit tied to any stat: he perches on the leading bar at seg1:mid, seg2:mid, seg3:start and simply stays there.
The mascot renders upside-down/head-down from seg3:end through payoff@-0.4, and is clipped behind the closing caption box at seg4:start.
The source line collides with the 'Buybacks'/'Dividends' axis labels in seg2:mid through payoff@-0.4, and a second duplicate source line sits outside the card at seg4:start.
In seg3:start the 2021 columns occupy only the bottom 40% of the plot, leaving the upper half as empty grey track.
fixes: Open on the 2025 trillion-dollar bar already blowing past the frame, then rewind to 2007 — put the payoff first instead of building bars from empty.
